link.title: Deriving the Gradient for the Backward Pass of Layer Normalization

entry.content:
Forward Pass Recap

First, let’s write down the forward pass for a single input vector \(x\) (a row from \(X\)) of dimension \(N\):

\[y = rac{x - \mu}{\sqrt{\sigma^2 + \epsilon}} * \gamma + eta\]

We can break down the forward pass into the following steps:

  1. Mean: \(\mu = rac{1}{N} \sum_j x_j\)
  2. Variance: \(\sigma^2 = rac{1}{N} \sum_j (x_j - \mu)^2\)
  3. Inverse Standard Deviation (rstd): \( ext{rstd} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\sigma^2 + \epsilon}}\)
  4. Normalized Input (\(\hat{x}\)): \( egin{equation} \hat{x}_j = (x_j - \mu) \cdot ext{rstd} \label{eq:1} \end{equation}\)
  5. Output (\(y\)): \( egin{equation} y_j = \hat{x}_j \cdot \gamma_j + eta_j \label{eq:2} \end{equation}\)

In general for ML applications, while doing the backward pass, we are given \( rac{dL}{dy_j}\) (denoted as \(dy_j\)) which is the gradient of the loss \(L\) with respect to the output \(y_j\).

We want to find \( rac{dL}{dx_j}\) (denoted \(dx_j\)), \( rac{dL}{d\gamma_j}\) (denoted \(d\gamma_j\)), and \( rac{dL}{d eta_j}\) (denoted \(d eta_j\)).

Gradients \( rac{dL}{d\gamma_j}\) and \( rac{dL}{d eta_j}\)

These are the simplest. \(\gamma_j\) and \( eta_j\) only affect \(y_j\) directly in the final step.

Let’s define \(\delta_{kj}\) as 1 if \(k=j\), and \(0\) otherwise.

\[ rac{\partial y_k}{\partial \gamma_j} = \hat{x}_j \delta_{kj}\] \[ rac{\partial y_k}{\partial eta_j} = \delta_{kj}\]

Using the chain rule:

\[ rac{dL}{d\gamma_j} = \sum_k \left( rac{dL}{dy_k} rac{\partial y_k}{\partial \gamma_j} ight) = rac{dL}{dy_j} rac{\partial y_j}{\partial \gamma_j} = dy_j \cdot \hat{x}_j\] \[ rac{dL}{d eta_j} = \sum_k \left( rac{dL}{dy_k} rac{\partial y_k}{\partial eta_j} ight) = rac{dL}{dy_j} rac{\partial y_j}{\partial eta_j} = dy_j \cdot 1\]

If we consider the whole batch (multiple rows), \(\gamma_j\) and \( eta_j\) are shared. So, the gradients are summed over all rows \(i\):

\[ rac{dL}{d\gamma_j} = \sum_i (dy_{ij} \cdot \hat{x}_{ij})\] \[ rac{dL}{d eta_j} = \sum_i dy_{ij}\]

Gradient \( rac{dL}{d\hat{x}_j}\)

From Equation \eqref{eq:2}:

\[ rac{\partial y_k}{\partial \hat{x}_j} = \gamma_j \delta_{kj}\]

So,

\[ egin{equation} rac{dL}{d\hat{x}_j} = \sum_k \left( rac{dL}{dy_k} rac{\partial y_k}{\partial \hat{x}_j} ight) = rac{dL}{dy_j} rac{\partial y_j}{\partial \hat{x}_j} = dy_j \cdot \gamma_j \label{eq:3} \end{equation}\]

Gradient \( rac{dL}{dx_j}\) (The Core Part)

This is the most complex part because \(x_j\) affects all \(\hat{x}_k\) in the same row through \(\mu\) and \( ext{rstd}\).

We need \( rac{dL}{dx_j} = \sum_k \left( rac{dL}{d\hat{x}_k} rac{\partial \hat{x}_k}{\partial x_j} ight)\).

We already have \( rac{dL}{d\hat{x}_k} = dy_k \cdot \gamma_k\) (from Equation \eqref{eq:3}). Let’s call this \(d\hat{x}'_k\).

Now we need \( rac{\partial \hat{x}_k}{\partial x_j}\). Recall (from Equation \eqref{eq:1}), \(\hat{x}_k = (x_k - \mu) \cdot ext{rstd}\).

Using the product rule:

\( rac{\partial \hat{x}_k}{\partial x_j} = rac{\partial (x_k - \mu)}{\partial x_j} \cdot ext{rstd} + (x_k - \mu) \cdot rac{\partial ext{rstd}}{\partial x_j}\).

Let’s find the intermediate derivatives:

\[ rac{\partial \mu}{\partial x_j} = rac{1}{N}\] \[ rac{\partial (x_k - \mu)}{\partial x_j} = rac{\partial x_k}{\partial x_j} - rac{\partial \mu}{\partial x_j} = \delta_{kj} - rac{1}{N}\]

Next, \( rac{\partial ext{rstd}}{\partial x_j}\):

\[ ext{rstd} = (\sigma^2 + \epsilon)^{- rac{1}{2}}\] \[ rac{\partial ext{rstd}}{\partial x_j} = - rac{1}{2} (\sigma^2 + \epsilon)^{- rac{3}{2}} rac{\partial \sigma^2}{\partial x_j}\] \[ egin{equation} rac{\partial ext{rstd}}{\partial x_j} = - rac{1}{2} ext{rstd}^3 rac{\partial \sigma^2}{\partial x_j} \label{eq:4} \end{equation}\]

Now, \( rac{\partial \sigma^2}{\partial x_j}\):

\[\sigma^2 = rac{1}{N} \sum_p (x_p - \mu)^2\] \[ rac{\partial \sigma^2}{\partial x_j} = rac{1}{N} \sum_p \left[ 2 (x_p - \mu) \cdot rac{\partial (x_p - \mu)}{\partial x_j} ight]\] \[ rac{\partial \sigma^2}{\partial x_j} = rac{2}{N} \sum_p \left[ (x_p - \mu) \cdot \left(\delta_{pj} - rac{1}{N} ight) ight]\] \[ rac{\partial \sigma^2}{\partial x_j} = rac{2}{N} \left[ (x_j - \mu)\left(1 - rac{1}{N} ight) + \sum_{p eq j} (x_p - \mu)\left(- rac{1}{N} ight) ight]\] \[ rac{\partial \sigma^2}{\partial x_j} = rac{2}{N} \left[ (x_j - \mu) - rac{1}{N}(x_j - \mu) - rac{1}{N}\sum_{p eq j} (x_p - \mu) ight]\] \[ rac{\partial \sigma^2}{\partial x_j} = rac{2}{N} \left[ (x_j - \mu) - rac{1}{N}\sum_p (x_p - \mu) ight]\]

Since \(\sum_p (x_p - \mu) = 0\), the second term vanishes.

\[ egin{equation} rac{\partial \sigma^2}{\partial x_j} = rac{2}{N} (x_j - \mu) \label{eq:5} \end{equation}\]

Substitute back into Equation \eqref{eq:4}, \( rac{\partial ext{rstd}}{\partial x_j}\):

\[ rac{\partial ext{rstd}}{\partial x_j} = \left(- rac{1}{2} ight) \cdot ext{rstd}^3 \cdot \left( rac{2}{N} ight) \cdot (x_j - \mu)\] \[ rac{\partial ext{rstd}}{\partial x_j} = - rac{1}{N} ext{rstd}^3 (x_j - \mu)\] \[ rac{\partial ext{rstd}}{\partial x_j} = - rac{1}{N} ext{rstd}^2 \cdot ((x_j - \mu) \cdot ext{rstd})\] \[ egin{equation} rac{\partial ext{rstd}}{\partial x_j} = - rac{1}{N} ext{rstd}^2 \hat{x}_j \label{eq:6} \end{equation}\]

Now assemble \( rac{\partial \hat{x}_k}{\partial x_j}\):

\[ rac{\partial \hat{x}_k}{\partial x_j} = \left(\delta_{kj} - rac{1}{N} ight) \cdot ext{rstd} + (x_k - \mu) \cdot \left(- rac{1}{N} ext{rstd}^2 \hat{x}_j ight)\] \[ rac{\partial \hat{x}_k}{\partial x_j} = \left(\delta_{kj} - rac{1}{N} ight) \cdot ext{rstd} - rac{1}{N} \cdot ((x_k - \mu) \cdot ext{rstd}) \cdot ext{rstd} \cdot \hat{x}_j\] \[ rac{\partial \hat{x}_k}{\partial x_j} = \left(\delta_{kj} - rac{1}{N} ight) \cdot ext{rstd} - rac{1}{N} \hat{x}_k \cdot ext{rstd} \cdot \hat{x}_j\] \[ egin{equation} rac{\partial \hat{x}_k}{\partial x_j} = rac{ ext{rstd}}{N} (N \delta_{kj} - 1 - \hat{x}_k \hat{x}_j) \label{eq:7} \end{equation}\]

Finally, using Equation \eqref{eq:7},

\[ rac{dL}{dx_j} = \sum_k \left( d\hat{x}'_k \cdot rac{\partial \hat{x}_k}{\partial x_j} ight)\] \[ rac{dL}{dx_j} = \sum_k \left[ d\hat{x}'_k \cdot rac{ ext{rstd}}{N} (N \delta_{kj} - 1 - \hat{x}_k \hat{x}_j) ight]\] \[ rac{dL}{dx_j} = rac{ ext{rstd}}{N} \sum_k \left[ d\hat{x}'_k (N \delta_{kj} - 1 - \hat{x}_k \hat{x}_j) ight]\] \[ rac{dL}{dx_j} = rac{ ext{rstd}}{N} \left[ (d\hat{x}'_j (N - 1 - \hat{x}_j \hat{x}_j)) + \sum_{k eq j} d\hat{x}'_k (-1 - \hat{x}_k \hat{x}_j) ight]\] \[ rac{dL}{dx_j} = rac{ ext{rstd}}{N} \left[ N d\hat{x}'_j - d\hat{x}'_j - d\hat{x}'_j \hat{x}_j^2 - \sum_{k eq j} d\hat{x}'_k - \sum_{k eq j} (d\hat{x}'_k \hat{x}_k \hat{x}_j) ight]\] \[ rac{dL}{dx_j} = rac{ ext{rstd}}{N} \left[ N d\hat{x}'_j - \left(\sum_k d\hat{x}'_k ight) - \hat{x}_j \left(\sum_k d\hat{x}'_k \hat{x}_k ight) ight]\]

The sum expansions are correct because \(d\hat{x}'_j \hat{x}_j^2\) is one term of \(\hat{x}_j (\sum_k d\hat{x}'_k \hat{x}_k)\) and \(d\hat{x}'_j\) is one term of \(\sum_k d\hat{x}'_k\).

So, for a specific \(j\), from Equation \eqref{eq:8}:

\[ egin{equation} rac{dL}{dx_j} = ext{rstd} \cdot \left[ d\hat{x}'_j - rac{1}{N} \left(\sum_k d\hat{x}'_k ight) - rac{\hat{x}_j}{N} \left(\sum_k d\hat{x}'_k \hat{x}_k ight) ight] \label{eq:8} \end{equation}\]

Now:

  • \(d\hat{x}'_j = dy_j \cdot \gamma_j\) (from Equation \eqref{eq:3})
  • Let \(c_2 = rac{1}{N} \sum_k d\hat{x}'_k = rac{1}{N} \sum_k (dy_k \cdot \gamma_k)\)
  • Let \(c_1 = rac{1}{N} \sum_k (d\hat{x}'_k \cdot \hat{x}_k) = rac{1}{N} \sum_k ( (dy_k \cdot \gamma_k) \cdot \hat{x}_k )\)

Substituting these back in Equation \eqref{eq:8}:

\[ rac{dL}{dx_j} = ext{rstd} \cdot \left[ (dy_j \cdot \gamma_j) - c_2 - \hat{x}_j \cdot c_1 ight]\] \[ egin{equation} rac{dL}{dx_j} = ext{rstd} \cdot \left[ (dy_j \cdot \gamma_j) - (\hat{x}_j \cdot c_1 + c_2) ight] \label{eq:9} \end{equation}\]

If we want to be more explicit with batch indexing (let \(i\) be the row/sequence index in the batch):

\[ egin{equation} rac{dL}{dx_{ij}} = ext{rstd}_i \cdot \left[ (dy_{ij} \cdot \gamma_j) - c_{2_{i}} - \hat{x}_{ij} \cdot c_{1_{i}} ight] \label{eq:10} \end{equation}\]

We now have the final gradients -

\[ oxed{ egin{aligned} rac{dL}{d\gamma_j} &= \sum_i (dy_{ij} \cdot \hat{x}_{ij}) \ rac{dL}{d eta_j} &= \sum_i dy_{ij} \ rac{dL}{dx_{ij}} &= ext{rstd}_i \cdot \left[ (dy_{ij} \cdot \gamma_j) - c_{2_{i}} - \hat{x}_{ij} \cdot c_{1_{i}} ight] \end{aligned} }\]

where,

\[ oxed{ egin{aligned} c_1 = rac{1}{N} \sum_k (d\hat{x}'_k \cdot \hat{x}_k) &= rac{1}{N} \sum_k ( (dy_k \cdot \gamma_k) \cdot \hat{x}_k ) \ c_2 = rac{1}{N} \sum_k d\hat{x}'_k &= rac{1}{N} \sum_k (dy_k \cdot \gamma_k) \ d\hat{x}'_j &= dy_j \cdot \gamma_j \end{aligned} }\]
